kmer-dust · chr21 · 24 assemblies · measured, not simulated

Pairing landmarks makes satellite DNA legible

A single FracMinHash hash is order-blind: inside an alpha-satellite array the same 31-mer recurs hundreds of times, so a match says almost nothing about where. Hash landmarks in pairs, carrying the gap between them, and each token becomes local context instead of a lone word — the trick Shazam uses to find a song from six seconds of noise. Everything below is computed from real HPRC release-2 assemblies.

Correspondence, recovered without an aligner

Every shared token votes for an offset: where its position in the HPRC haplotype sits relative to its position in CHM13. A true correspondence makes the votes line up into a horizontal band that steps as indels accumulate. Votes agreeing with their local modal offset (±10 kb over a 100 kb window) are collinear; the rest are stray. Drag to pan, scroll to zoom, double-click to reset.

Reading the repeat period straight off the sketch

Crystallography's Patterson function, imported. Treat retained hashes as a labelled point process on the chromosome and histogram the distances between same-hash pairs: peaks sit at the recurring distances of the structure. No monomer library, no period prior, no alignment. Grey guides mark multiples of the 171 bp alpha-satellite monomer. Hover to read a lag; the panel below scans the same array across all 24 haplotypes.

Where the gain comes from

Mean multiplicity of a token within CHM13 chr21 — how many times the same token occurs, so lower is more specific. Pairing costs 3× the tokens; it buys specificity only where the sequence is repetitive, which is exactly where single hashes fail. In euchromatin it changes almost nothing, because there is nothing to fix.

featurehashessinglepairedgain

Built from results/chr21: 24 assemblies, k=31, scaled=200 (~1 retained hash per 202 bp). Tokens pair each landmark with the next 3, keyed by rank gap — the count of retained hashes between them, which an indel leaves unchanged unless it creates or destroys a landmark. Tokens occurring more than 40 times in either assembly are dropped, as Shazam drops over-common landmarks. Points are subsampled for the browser; the headline counts are the full totals.
